rationale: Following the investigator's choice of h2, the design is a cost-consequence analysis of the switch: six months before against six months after, costing nurse set-up time (claim c3), appointment time (claim c2) and repeat appointments for deferred eligibility decisions (claim c1), with usable diaries as a consequence and a separate three-year budget impact for injectable preventives (claim c4). A comparison of diary completeness is not repeated because it has a randomised answer (claim c5). Reporting follows CHEERS 2022.
alternatives: Comparison of app and paper diaries on completeness and decisions (set aside: answered by the crossover study and not the manager's question)
Cost-utility analysis (refused: no utility data and a six-month horizon)
guidelines: ISPOR budget impact analysis good practice
whyNotMoreComplex: A model of long-term migraine outcomes would need effects on headache days that the switch is not expected to produce by itself; observed costs and a transparent budget impact answer the decision.

decision.statement: Run a cost-consequence analysis of the January 2027 switch from paper to app diaries, comparing six months before with six months after on nurse set-up time, appointment length, repeat appointments for deferred eligibility decisions and preventive prescriptions, with a three-year budget impact estimate for injectable preventives.
decision.question: What does switching the clinic to app diaries cost and save, and what does it do to the preventive budget?

criteria.text: Missing diaries generate costed clinic activity that the switch could reduce.
The switch has measurable new costs and a large consequence in the drug budget.
Diary completeness with the app is unknown and must be established first.

gates.requirement: Research office classification of the evaluation
gates.evidence: Service evaluation reference SE-NEU-2026-15 dated 2026-09-09, supplied by the investigator

gates.requirement: Access to diary completeness data from the digital health service
gates.evidence: Agreement DHS-2026-44, supplied by the investigator

alternatives: Comparison of app and paper diary completeness and decision quality (the model's first pick, set aside by the investigator)
decision.note: Rests on ledger claims c1 to c4 from retrieved records; c5 shows that the completeness question already has a randomised answer.

summary: Cost-consequence analysis with a budget impact estimate; the decision rests on four ledger claims and both gates are met.
